prompt: Put the stages of an agency project in order.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.
task.explanation: Agree what to build, design it, build and test it, let the client accept it, launch, then support it.

prompt: The client has a 20-hour monthly support retainer. Work out what's left this month.

task.explanation: 15 of 20 hours used = 75%; 5 hours left. Tell the client before it runs out.

prompt: A critical bug is reported in the live app. Put the hotfix steps in order.

task.prompt: Drag the items into the right order, first at the top.

items.label: Create a hotfix branch from the production code
Merge the fix back into the development branch
Reproduce the bug and confirm its severity
Fix it and get a code review

task.explanation: Confirm first, fix from what is live, review and test, release, then merge back so the next release does not reintroduce the bug.

prompt: Launch is Monday. In Thursday's UAT the client finds discount codes fail at checkout, plus six cosmetic issues.

task.prompt: Choose the best option at each step.

steps.question: What do you do first?
options: Fix everything before Monday, whatever it takes.
Triage with the client: agree which issues block launch.
Launch anyway; UAT is just a formality.
Postpone launch by a month.
steps.explanation: Not every UAT finding is a blocker. Agree severity with the client before planning.

steps.question: The discount fix needs two days of work and testing. What do you offer?
options: Launch Monday with broken discount codes and say nothing.
A short delay, or launch with discount codes off; the client decides in writing.
Skip testing the fix to make Monday.
Promise the fix by Friday night.
steps.explanation: Give the client a real choice with trade-offs and record the decision.

steps.question: What happens to the six cosmetic issues?
options: Ignore them.
Log them for a post-launch patch with an agreed date.
Block the launch until all are fixed.
Ask the client to fix them.
steps.explanation: Minor issues go into a scheduled patch so they are not forgotten.

prompt: A client asks if this pull request can go out in today's release. Flag what blocks the merge.

task.prompt: Flag the rows that are a problem, then answer the question.
task.title: PR #212 Fix discount code rounding

questions.question: Can it ship today?
options: Yes, merge it now.
Only after the tests pass and it is approved.
Yes, if an admin overrides the checks.
questions.explanation: Failing tests and no review mean it is not ready; overriding checks to hit a date is how bugs reach production.

prompt: On Wednesday, Apple rejects the client's app because the reviewer had no demo login. The client's marketing launch is set for Friday.

task.prompt: Choose the best option at each step.

steps.question: What do you do today?
options: Wait until Friday to see what happens.
Tell the client today, add demo credentials to the review notes and resubmit.
Appeal the rejection and do nothing else.
Publish on the website instead.
steps.explanation: Tell the client the same day and fix the cause quickly. A missing demo account is a common, easy fix.

steps.question: What do you advise about Friday?
options: Guarantee approval by Friday.
Review time isn't guaranteed: hold the marketing launch until approval, or have a fallback date.
Cancel the launch entirely.
Launch marketing anyway; the link will work eventually.
steps.explanation: The agency doesn't control App Store review time, so never promise a date that depends on it.

steps.question: How do you prevent this next time?
options: Use a pre-submission checklist (demo account, privacy details) and plan buffer days for review.
Submit on the launch day.
Ask Apple to skip review.
Only release on Android.
steps.explanation: A checklist and review buffer protect the launch date.

prompt: The release is due today. Review this pull request and flag what should stop it shipping.

task.prompt: Flag the rows that are a problem, then answer the question.
task.title: PR #348 Add push notification settings

rows.issue: The team marked it not ready: the client's text is missing.

cells: Adds a database change; not yet run on staging
rows.issue: An untested database change is a release risk.

questions.question: Green checks and an approval are present. Is it ready?
options: Yes; checks and approval are all that matter.
No: get the client copy, run the migration on staging, then merge.
Yes, if it is merged after office hours.
questions.explanation: Passing checks are necessary but not sufficient; labels and untested migrations matter too.

prompt: Friday 18:00: after today's release, card payments fail for 30% of users.

task.prompt: Choose the best option at each step.

steps.question: What is the best immediate action?
options: Roll back to the previous version, if it is safe to, and tell the client.
Keep the release and fix forward over the weekend.
Wait until Monday to investigate.
Turn off the whole app.
steps.explanation: When payments fail, restore the last good version fast. Roll back only if no irreversible change, like a data migration, prevents it.

steps.question: The client wants the new feature back on Monday. What do you agree?
options: Redeploy the same build on Monday.
Find the root cause, fix and test on staging, then release with a short incident note.
Release only on Fridays from now on.
Drop the feature permanently.
steps.explanation: A root cause and a tested fix, explained in a short incident note, rebuild confidence.

prompt: Who carries out user acceptance testing (UAT) on an agency project?

options: Only the agency's developers
The client, or users they choose, checking it meets their needs
The app store
Nobody; it is optional
mcq.explanation: UAT is the client's check that the work meets what was agreed before go-live.

options: The project's end date
A shared checklist every item must meet to count as finished
The final invoice
The client's sign-off email
mcq.explanation: It sets a shared quality bar (reviewed, tested, deployed to staging...) so 'done' means the same thing to everyone.

prompt: Why shouldn't a PM promise a client an exact date for a new mobile app to go live in the stores?

options: Apps cannot be released on weekdays
Store review time varies and can end in rejection
Developers never know when they will finish
Store listings must be written by the client
mcq.explanation: Apple and Google review every release; time varies and rejections happen, so plan a buffer.

prompt: The SOW includes a 30-day warranty for defects. In week two, the client asks for a new CSV export. What is it?

options: A warranty fix, done free
New work: a change request or support request
A hotfix
UAT feedback
mcq.explanation: A warranty covers things that do not work as agreed; new features are new scope.
